paper.title: Matching Markets meet Cumulative Prospect Theory: Towards Optimal and Adversarially Robust Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Human centric matching market with CPT regret
unmapped: Two-sided matching market: N players compete for K>=N arms; each arm has a known strict ranking over players and accepts its highest-ranked proposer; rejected players get 0 reward
Regret is player-optimal stable regret w.r.t. the player-optimal stable matching
Arms are evaluated by CPT-distorted values with an alpha-Holder probability weighting function w (constant L); the learner uses w, L, alpha and M
settings.definition_quote: We study a two-sided market comprising $N$ players ... and $K\!\ge\!N$ arms ... Each arm accepts its highest-ranked proposer under~$\pi_j$ ... The distorted utility of arm $a_j$ for player $p_i$ is defined as $\mu_{i,j}=\int_{0}^{\infty} w(\mathbb{P}(Y_{i,j} > z)) dz - \int_{0}^{\infty} w(\mathbb{P}(-Y_{i,j} > z)) dz$.

settings.name_in_paper: Corrupted matching market with CPT regret, known corruption budget

algorithms.name: CPT-ETGS with enlarged confidence intervals (known corruption)

symbols.L_h: Holder constant of the weighting function w
symbols.Delta_pref: minimum CPT preference gap among the first N+1 ranked arms over all players
symbols.Delta_imax: mu_{i,m_i^*}, CPT value of player i's player-optimal stable arm

conditions: CPT-distorted player-optimal stable regret of each player (expected, via distorted gaps)
w is alpha-Holder with constant L, w(0)=0, w(1)=1

source.label: th:cpt_etgs
source.quote: The player optimal stable regret incurred by each $p_i \in \mathcal{N}$ under Algorithm~\ref{alg:cpt_etgs} satisfies \mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)] \le c_0 \left( \frac{3K\log T}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}} \left(4LM\right)^{2/\alpha} + N^2 + 2NK \right)\Delta_{i,\max}. where $c_0$ is a universal positive constant.

results.notes: Quantity is CPT-distorted regret (risk-aware) so recorded as 'other'; comparator is the player-optimal stable matching (mapped to best_policy loosely). Canonical alpha/L symbols renamed since they mean Holder parameters.

symbols.Delta_i: CPT preference gap Delta_{1,m_1^*,j} of player 1 between its optimal arm and arm j

conditions: exists an instance with serial dictatorship (all arms share ranking p_1 > ... > p_N)
reduction to single-player CPT bandit lower bound (Kolla et al., Theorem 3) for uniformly efficient algorithms

source.label: lemma:lower_bound
source.quote: There exists a problem instance with serial dictatorship such that for any learning algorithm, the player-optimal stable regret of player $p_1$ satisfies \liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{\mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_1(T)]}{\log T} \ge \sum_{j \in [K], j \neq m_1^*} \frac{1}{4}(LM)^{2/\alpha} \left( \frac{1}{\Delta_{1,m_1^*,j}} \right)^{\frac{2}{\alpha}-1}.

results.notes: Statement says 'any learning algorithm' but proof invokes the result for uniformly efficient algorithms, so recorded as uniformly_good. Essentially a restatement of Kolla et al. via reduction.

bound.expression_latex: c_1\!\left(\sum_{j \in [K], j \neq m_i^*}\log T \,\frac{(LM)^{2/\alpha}}{\Delta_{i,m_i^*,j}^{2/\alpha - 1}} + N^2 \log T \, \frac{(LM)^{2/\alpha}}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}} \cdot \Delta_{i,\max}\right)

symbols.Delta_i: CPT preference gap Delta_{i,m_i^*,j} of player i between its stable arm and arm j
symbols.Delta_pref: minimum preference gap among first N+1 arms over all players

source.label: th:improved
source.quote: The player-optimal stable regret for each player $p_i$ satisfies \mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)] \le c_1\!\left(\sum_{j \in [K], j \neq m_i^*}\log T \,\frac{(LM)^{2/\alpha}}{\Delta_{i,m_i^*,j}^{2/\alpha - 1}} + N^2 \log T \, \frac{(LM)^{2/\alpha}}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}} \cdot \Delta_{i,\max}\right) where $c_1$ is a universal positive constant.

results.notes: Sum is over arms j != m_i^*, which may include arms preferred to m_i^* (negative gaps in the regret sense); recorded with sum_subopt. Paper claims matching lower bound when K >> N.

symbols.Delta_pref: minimum preference gap among first N+1 arms over all players

conditions: per-player corruption budget sum_t max_j |r_ij(t) - r^S_ij(t)| <= C known
stochastic rewards in [0,M], corrupted rewards non-negative

source.label: th:known
source.quote: With a (known) corruption budget of $C$, the CPT regret of $p_i \in \mathcal{N}$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)]=\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{K\log T}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}}+ K\left(\frac{C}{\Delta}\right)^{1/\alpha}\right)$.

results.notes: O hides L, M, N and Delta_{i,max} factors (proof bound multiplies by Delta_{i,max} and includes N^2, NK terms).

symbols.Delta_pref: minimum preference gap among first N+1 arms over all players
symbols.d_sub: sub-phase length parameter d of the algorithm (chosen so that d log T + 2 <= 2 d log T)

conditions: stochastic rewards in [0,M], corrupted rewards non-negative
tuning: log T layers, layer l sampled with probability 2^{-l}
sub-phase length d with d log T + 2 <= 2 d log T

source.label: th:unknown
source.quote: The CPT-Multi-layer ETGS race algorithm achieves the player-optimal stable regret upper bound of each player $p_i$, $\mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)]$ as \mathcal{O}\!\left(\left[KC\left(\log^2T\right)\left(\frac{LM}{\Delta}\right)^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}+K(\log T+C)(\log T)^{1+\frac{1}{\alpha}}\left(\frac{dL}{\Delta}\right)^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}\right]\Delta_{i,\max}\right).

results.notes: d is an algorithm parameter (sub-phase length), renamed d_sub to avoid clash with canonical dimension d.
